1. The present complaint is filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as PFA Act), alleging that the accused have violated the provisions of the PFA Act and Rules.

2. As per the complaint, on 12.08.2008 at about 3:00 pm, Food Inspector Bal Mukand purchased a sample of "Dal Chana", an article of food for analysis from accused No. 1 Raj Kumar Gupta, who was Da vs Raj Kumar Gupta Etc on 8 May, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174923594/

sentences.text: the vendor cum partner of M/s Gupta Store, 47, Gole Market New Delhi -110001, where the said food article was found stored for sale and where accused No. 1 Raj Kumar was found vending the article of food at the time of taking the sample.
The sample consisted of approx. 1500 gms of "Dal Chana" (ready for sale) taken from an open plastic bag bearing no label declaration.
The sample was taken under the supervision/direction of Sh. Tej Singh, SDM/LHA.
The sample was taken after proper mixing with the help of clean a dry jhaba by rotating it in all possible directions.
Food inspector divided the sample of the article of food into three equal parts then and there by putting it into three clean and dry glass bottles.

Each bottle containing the sample was separately packed,
fastened and sealed according to the PFA Act, 1954 & Rules, 1955.
The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and wrapper of the bottles containing the sample.
Notice in Form VI was given to accused No.1 Raj Kumar and the price of sample was also paid to him vide vendor receipt dated DA vs Raj Kumar Gupta etc 12-08-2008.

sentences.text: Panchnama too was prepared at the spot.
All the documents prepared by the Food Inspector were signed by accused No. 1 Raj Kumar and by the other witness Sh. Naubat Singh, FA.
Before taking the sample efforts were made to get the public witnesses to join the proceedings but none came forward, as such Sh. Naubat Singh, FA was joined as witness.

3. One counter-part of the sample bearing LHA Code Number 33/LHA/22273 in intact condition along with copy of memo in Form VII and another copy of memo in Form Vll under sealed cover were sent separately to the Public Analyst, Delhi and two counterparts of the sample along with two copies of memos in Form VI were deposited with the SDM/LHA in intact conditions.
All copies of Memos in Form VII bear the seal impression with which sample parts were sealed.
Public Analyst analysed the sample and found the sample to be not conforming to standard.

The report of Public Analyst is as follows:
"The sample is adulterated because it is insect infecsted with living insects which are four in number."
4.

1 Raj Kumar Gupta accused No.2 Puran Lal Gupta and none is a sleeping or non- working partner as per reply of STD Ward No.3, as such both the partners were incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the said firm.
Being a partnership firm M/s DA vs Raj Kumar Gupta etc Gupta Store is also liable.

sentences.text: 5. Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA.
The complaint was then filed in the court on 18.09.2009 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(a)(f)&(m) of PFA Act, 1954 as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act against the accused.
6. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 18.09.2009.

On the basis of PA report as well as evidence led in pre-charge evidence, charge was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1) (a) PFA Act being violation of 2(ia)(a)(f)&(m) of PFA Act, 1954, to which accused person pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
7. At the trial, the prosecution examined three witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 FI Bal Mukand, PW-2 FA Naubat Singh, and PW-3 SDM/LHA B.K. Jha.
PW-1 and PW-4 were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh. Tej Singh(since expired).

These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample commodity of "Daal Chana" 1500 gms from the vendor for analysis,
bearing no label or declaration, the sample of daal chana taken from the entire mixed lot, dividing the sample into three equal parts by putting them into three separate clean and DA vs Raj Kumar Gupta etc dry sample bottles, separately sealing, packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses.
They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex.PW-1/A, Notice in form VI Ex. PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex.PW-1/C and raid report Ex.PW1/C-1.
Thereafter, on 13.08.2008 one counterpart of the sample along with one copy of memo in form VII and another copy of memo in form VII in sealed deposited with PA vide receipt Ex.PW1/D.

The remaining two counter parts of the sample in intact condition along with two copies of memo of Form VII in a sealed packet were deposited with LHA vide LHA Receipt Ex.PW1/E under intimation that one counterpart of the same has already been deposited with PA.

Thereafter,
on receipt of the PA report Ex.PW1/F according to which sample was found adulterated.

The then Director PFA granted his Consent for prosecution vide sanction order Ex.PW1/O.
Thereafter, the present complaint Ex. PW1/P was filed before the Court.
Then intimation letter Ex.PW1/Q alongwith copy of PA reports was sent to the accused vide postal receipt ExPW1/R.
These witnesses were duly cross-examined by Ld. Defence Counsel.
8. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC was recorded wherein the accused denied the allegations and pleaded innocence.
The accused chooses not to lead defence evidence accordingly the matter was fixed for final arguments.
9. In a criminal case, the burden is on the prosecution to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt by leading positive evidence.
This burden cannot be shifted to the accused and it has to be necessary discharged by the prosecution itself.
10. It is to be understood that the present is a case of adulteration in DA vs Raj Kumar Gupta etc the sample of Dal Chana on the ground that the sample had four living insects as per the PA report.

sentences.text: 11.The main defence of the accused is that these insects were not there when the sample was lifted because it has come in the cross examination of the witnesses of the prosecution that the insects were not visible when the sample was taken.

It was contended that these insects may have developed at some later stage as the sample was analyzed by PA from 13.08.2008 to 20/08/2008 and it took around 8 days to analyse the sample.
12.

Since the insects was not visible at the sampling as per the deposition of the prosecution witnesses, it cannot be ruled out that these four insects found in the sample, may have developed later on also.

5 13.

In State of Maharastra vs Jathala Devshi & Ors relied upon by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Delhi Administration vs Sunil Kumar in Crl.A 59/2006 dated 28.01.2014, it was held that - "Mr.
Ganatra rightly urges that there must be evidence to show that these insects were present on the date the sample was taken.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He contends that if living larvae were visible to the naked eye of the analyst, the Food Inspector who collected the sample on 09.01.1973, ought to have also seen them and in as much as he has made no such note, the report would be insufficient to hold that such insects were present when the sample was collected."
14.

It was further observed in the case DA vs Sunil Kumar (supra) that - "In (1975), 1 FAC 281 in Mukund Lal vs State where a DA vs Raj Kumar Gupta etc sample of maggajkddu remained unexamined and unalyayzed for 12 to 13 days it was held that there was a possibility that the sample become infested with insects during that period.

The court had reiterated that the possibility of the sample food article being infested with insects after it was purchased by the Food Inspector in the intervening period cannot be ruled out it was noted that an egg normally takes 1 to 14 days to develop into an insect; larvae are a second stage of eggs and their incubation is 4 to 7 days; the presence of eggs in an article cannot make the article of food insect infested.

Thus, the arguments of the learned counsel for respondents that the eggs in the instant case after the seizure of sample "aata" had developed into insects in this intervening period of 11 days cannot be ruled out this is also clear from the deposition of the witnesses as noted above.
There was admittedly no positive evidence that Food Inspector had seen living worms or insects at the time of taking the sample.
It is also an admitted position that the incubation period for an egg to become an insect is 14 days; for larvae which is the second stage it is 4-7 days.
18. Sample in this case was analysed after 11 days.
Larvae having matured into insects in this intervening period as noted supra was not ruled out by any positive evidence.
It was bounden duty of the prosecution to rule out this possibility by producing expert opinion on the file which has not been done.
Benefit of this must accrue to the accused"
15. Further, there is no opinion of the CFL that the presence of the insects has made the sampling aata unfit for consumption.

In New Delhi Municipal Committee vs Chaman Lal and the State Crl Rev No. 40/1977 dated 22.01.1980, it was observed by the Delhi DA vs Raj Kumar Gupta etc High Court that an article of food would be insect infested if it has been attacked by insects in swarms or numbers.

entities.text: New Delhi Municipal Committee vs Chaman Lal and the State Crl Rev No. 40/1977
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Delhi DA vs Raj Kumar Gupta etc High Court
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Court held that presence of three living insects in a sample of 250 grms can by no scratch of imagination be called insect infested.
In the present case also the number of insects present was not large and therefore the sample cannot be said to be insect infested.

Reference may also be had to the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in State (Delhi Administration) vs Puran Mal Crl Appeal No. 539/1984 dated 26.03.1985, Shri Raghubir Sharan vs State Crl Rev No. 148/1969 dated 21.04.1971,
Food Inspector vs Harikesh Gupta Crl LP No. 744/2013 dated 23.05.2014, Ghansham Das vs The State of Haryana, Crl Rev No. 1200/1980 dated 17.05.1983 and State vs Anil Kumar Sodhi & Anr 2009(2) JCC 904, in favour of the accused.
